title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
summary: Deriving classes with a base class, calling base constructors, virtual and override, abstract classes and members, sealed, polymorphism through base-class references, protected members, type checks with is and as, and when composition is better than inheritance.

cards.q: What is the difference between abstract and virtual?
cards.a:
An abstract member has no body and must be overridden; a virtual one has a body that may be

`abstract` declares a member with no body that every concrete derived class must override. `virtual` gives a default body that derived classes may replace.

cards.q: Can you write new Shape("x") when Shape is abstract?
cards.a:
No: an abstract class cannot be instantiated, only derived from

An abstract class's constructor exists for derived classes to call with `base(...)`; you can only create objects of a derived, non-abstract class.

cards.q: `Shape s = new Circle(1);` `Area` is virtual and overridden in Circle. Which Area runs for `s.Area()`?
cards.a:
Circle's, because the object is a Circle

Virtual calls use the type of the actual object, not of the variable.
